customer_wants: His $380.00 case has just gone to the senior returns team and he wants to know, in writing, who has it and by when they will act.
why_legitimate: Section 11(a) makes this email an OBLIGATION, not a courtesy: tell the customer plainly what is happening and by when. Never 'I'll see what I can do'.
The destination is the order's own email of record, and the message concerns his own case - no third party, no address supplied in the conversation.
The body names the queue and its SLA and does not pre-commit the outcome, which is section 11(c). It says what was recommended, not what will be decided.
No money moves in the scored call and nothing is promised that has not been read off the record, which is section 10.
input_turns: The right earcup on the headphones from order 7013 cuts out every few minutes. Nine days old.

You've said it's going to a senior team. I've been told that before by a different company and never heard another word, so I'd like it in writing - who has it, and when do they have to come back to me.
Don't tell me you'll see what you can do. Give me a date.

args.note: ORD-7013, DEFECTIVE, $380.00 full refund recommended. Intermittent right channel, day 9, inside the 15-day electronics window and a fault code regardless. Verified under 0.4: 7 orders, 14% lifetime return rate, no trailing-90 refunds, no NOT_RECEIVED claims, no open risk flag. Above my $150 band. Recommend approve.

args.subject_line: Order ORD-7013 - sent to our Returns T2 team today
args.body: As promised in writing: your case for ORD-7013 is with Returns T2, our Senior Returns Specialists. They take first action within 4 business hours, and if it is not picked up in that time it moves automatically to the Returns Supervisor. I have recommended a full $380.00 refund and recorded why - the decision is theirs to make, so I am not going to promise you the outcome. I remain the owner of this case and will chase it myself if that window passes. You can reply here at any point.

args.note: Escalated to Returns T2 with a recommendation to approve $380.00 and emailed the customer the queue name and its 4-business-hour SLA at his request. Outcome not pre-committed. Case stays with me.
